commitResults.messageTitle: Level-0: Rename to saLLMan, add greeting and exit
commitResults.messageBody:
Rename the chatbot from the placeholder Duke to saLLMan, replacing the
banner with matching ASCII art and updating the docs. The bot now greets
the user and exits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-1: Echo user input until bye
commitResults.messageBody:
Read commands in a loop and echo them back, exiting on bye. Extract a
say() helper since every reply now shares the same divider formatting.

Keep entered text in a fixed-size array and print it numbered on the list
command, per the <=100 task assumption. Other input is stored rather than
echoed.

Track completion in a boolean array parallel to the task descriptions and
add a mark command. Extract formatTask() so list and mark share one status
format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-3: Reverse done status with unmark
commitResults.messageBody:
Add an unmark command mirroring mark, so a task wrongly marked done can be
set back to not done.

Replace the parallel description/status arrays with a Task object owning
both, moving status formatting into Task.toString(). Fields are protected
so Level-4 task types can inherit them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-4: Add todos, deadlines and events (A-Inheritance)
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce Todo, Deadline and Event subclasses of Task, each overriding
toString() to add its type icon and any date fields. Dates stay free text
for now. Unknown input no longer creates an untyped task.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-5: Handle the two basic input errors (minimal)
commitResults.messageBody:
Report a todo with no description and an unrecognised command instead of
mishandling them. Match a bare todo in its own branch so the missing
description is named rather than reported as an unknown command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-5: Handle all current error cases (typical)
commitResults.messageBody:
Split each input into command and arguments before dispatching, so a command
given without arguments reaches its own branch and can name what is missing.
Validate task numbers, deadline and event parts, and the full-list case.
Split on the bare /by and /from tokens so a missing description is diagnosed
correctly rather than reported as a missing delimiter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-5: Make error messages specific and actionable (stretch)
commitResults.messageBody:
Split the generic deadline and event errors into one message per failure, each
naming the missing part and pairing it with a worked example. Report the valid
task number range, and give an empty list its own message rather than telling
the user to pick from 1 to 0.

Replace the say-and-continue error blocks with a checked SallmanException
thrown from four validating parse methods and caught once in the main loop.
NumberFormatException is translated into a message phrased for the user.
Behaviour is unchanged; all 13 UI test cases still pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-6: Store tasks in an ArrayList (A-Collections)
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the fixed-size array and its separate taskCount with a List, so
remove() closes the gap and size() is always in step with the contents. Drops
the 100-task limit and its full-list error.

commitResults.messageTitle: A-Enums: Represent commands as an enum
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the chain of string comparisons with a Command enum and a switch, so
an unknown keyword is rejected once in fromKeyword() and every case is a known
command. The help text is now built from the constants, which stops it drifting
from the actual command set as it did when delete was added.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-7: Save tasks to disk and reload on startup
commitResults.messageBody:
The task list only existed in memory, so everything was lost when the
chatbot exited.

Add a Storage class that writes the list to a text file whenever it
changes and reads it back at startup. Each task renders itself via a
toFileFormat() method, mirroring how toString() already works, so the
subclasses stay responsible for their own fields.

The path is built with java.nio.file.Path so it works on any OS, and is
relative so the app is not tied to one computer. A missing data file
means a first run rather than an error, and the containing folder is
created on demand.

The data file path can be overridden by a command line argument. Without
it the UI tests would share, and overwrite, the real task list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-7: Survive a corrupted save file
commitResults.messageBody:
The loader trusted the data file completely, so a single damaged line
crashed the chatbot on startup with a stack trace and made every other
saved task unreachable. The file is plain text and invites hand editing,
so this is a realistic way to lose a task list.

Validate each line and skip only the ones that fail, keeping the rest.
Each rejection names the line number and the specific fault, so a
hand-edited file can be corrected rather than guessed at. Blank lines are
ignored silently, since a trailing newline is normal.

Checking the fields separately, rather than catching whatever exception
the parsing happens to throw, is what makes those specific messages
possible.

Add task persistence: the list is saved to a text file whenever it
changes, reloaded at startup, and a corrupted save file is repaired
rather than fatal.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-8: Parse dates instead of storing them as text
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and event dates were kept as whatever the user typed, so the
chatbot could not compare or reformat them, and "Sunday" was as valid as
a real date.

Store them as java.time.LocalDate. Dates are entered as yyyy-mm-dd and
shown back as MMM dd yyyy, e.g. 2019-10-15 is displayed as Oct 15 2019.
Both conversions live in a TaskDate helper so the two formats are defined
once rather than once per task type.

The data file keeps the input format rather than the display format, so
saved dates can be read back regardless of how they are shown.

This makes the chatbot stricter: text that is not a date is now refused,
where before it was accepted verbatim. That is the point of the
increment, but it does mean an existing data file with free-text dates
will have those lines reported as unreadable on the next start.

commitResults.messageTitle: Level-8: Add an on command to list tasks by date
commitResults.messageBody:
Storing real dates made it possible to ask questions about them, but
nothing did. Finding what is happening on a particular day meant reading
the whole list by eye.

Add "on <date>", which lists the deadlines due that day and the events
running over it. Each task type answers for itself through an isOn
method: a plain task is never on a date, a deadline matches its due
date, and an event matches any day it spans, not only its start and end.
Putting the test on the task rather than in the command keeps the
command from having to know which subclass it is looking at.

A date with nothing on it says so, rather than printing a heading with
nothing under it.

Give tasks real dates: deadlines and events now hold a LocalDate parsed
from yyyy-mm-dd and displayed as MMM dd yyyy, and an on command lists
whatever falls on a given day.
